title: 1. Hook: A Sudden Journey
text: Imagine sitting in a noisy, crowded city, surrounded by smoke and traffic. But in your memories, you are back in your beautiful village surrounded by green hills, flowing rivers, and thick forests. One day, you were told to pack everything and leave forever. How would that feel?

title: 2. Socratic Thinking: Why Leave?
text: Why do you think an entire village of people—who love their land, forests, and river—would suddenly pack their bags and leave their homes forever? What could force them to make such a heartbreaking choice?

content.title: 3. Discovery: The Building of a Dam
content.description: Watch how a peaceful river flowing through a village is blocked by a massive concrete wall. The water level rises, swallowing the trees, farms, and homes, leaving the villagers with no choice but to move.

title: 4. Reveal: The Meaning of Displacement
text: When people are forced to leave their homes, lands, and everything they know, often to make way for big projects like dams, highways, or factories, it is called displacement. Jatrya Bhai's family faced this when a dam was built across their river.

content.definition: The forced removal of people from their everyday environment or home, often due to large-scale construction projects.
A large barrier built across a river to hold back water, used for generating electricity or water supply.

content.question: Which of the following is the main reason Jatrya's family and others had to leave Khedi village?
options: They wanted to live in a big city.
A large dam was being built on their river.
They found better farming land elsewhere.

title: 6. Reflection: Was it a Fair Trade?
text: The government promised the villagers a new life with electricity, schools, and hospitals in a new place called Sinduri. But when they arrived, things were very different. If you were Jatrya, how would you explain your feelings to the city people who get electricity from the dam?

content.mistake: Thinking that displacement is the same as moving to a new house by choice.
content.correction: Displacement is forced. People do not want to leave, but they have to because their land is being taken away or destroyed.

title: 7. Connection: Life in the City
text: Displacement doesn't just mean moving houses. It changes everything. From the open spaces of Khedi to the tin sheds of Sinduri, and finally to the crowded, expensive streets of Mumbai. It connects to poverty, changes in livelihood (jobs), and cultural loss.

content.tip: Help students see the contrast. Ask them to compare the free firewood and natural food of Khedi with having to pay money for everything in Sinduri and Mumbai.

content.title: 8. Mastery: The Two Sides of Development
content.instructions: Create a simple T-chart in your notebook. On one side, list 3 benefits a big dam brings to a city. On the other side, list 3 problems it creates for the villagers living near the river. Share your chart with a friend!
